Subject: Proposal: lightweight hybrid pgvector + S3 tiering pilot with Redwood

Hi Vanessa + Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look — I'm Elena, Head of Partnerships at VectorFlow. We build an embeddable vector store that supports transparent S3 cold-tiering and a pgvector-compatible endpoint for customers who want a single failover path between managed and self-hosted storage. We've done a couple of pilots with inference vendors but wanted to propose a focused POC with Redwood to validate:

- seamless fallback from in-memory / warm index to S3 cold lane for large corpora,
- simple connector that exposes pgvector-compatible SQL for clients that prefer DB semantics,
- predictable cost curves under Redwood-style batching/kv-caching.

I've attached a short proposal (vectorflow-proposal.pdf) and a small sample schema and dataset snapshot (vf-sample-schema.csv). High-level POC ask: 4 weeks, success metrics around end-to-end 99th percentile query latency (target <120ms for warm reads, <350ms for cold reads) and a cost-per-query delta vs pure warm index under a 30% cold-hit ratio.

Are you available next week for a 30-min tech sync? We can put our engineering lead on the call to go over connector auth, replication, and fallback semantics.

Warmly,
Elena Torres

Thanks Vanessa — Thu 9/2 10:00am PT works for me. Confirmed on the calendar.

Elena / VectorFlow — to make the sync productive, can you please share the following ahead of the call (if available):
- representative API spec (auth types supported: API key, mTLS, OIDC?),
- sample SQL read/write flow for pgvector endpoint,
- expected QPS profile and max concurrent connections for the POC (our runtime needs to plan batching/worker sizing),
- size of the sample corpus you attached (rows, vector dim, avg tokens per doc),
- details on cold-tier retrieval latency (S3 region, presigning, parallel fetch strategy),
- any known constraints around KV cache/TTL interactions (we use aggressive prefix KV caching).

From Redwood side: our infra asks are usually minimal — a test API key for a POC tenant and a sample dataset (s3 or direct upload). We'll run an initial micro-benchmark using our const-batching profile to capture warm vs cold metrics. Typical POC flow we recommend:
1) Week 0: test credentials + baseline perf run (warm only)
2) Week 1: connector integration + small-scale traffic so we can validate correctness and auth
3) Week 2: load test to exercise cold-tier fallthrough and measure cost delta
4) Week 3: customer-facing evaluation and handoff + commercial MOU finalization

Also tagging some internal constraints so we can scope: our connector framework supports pgvector-compatible SQL and an adapter for S3 tiering, but we need to validate atomic consistency on reads under parallel batch merges. If VectorFlow can share a small sample of a production-like index (anonymized), that will accelerate week-0 validation.

Thanks — great list, Priyom. I've uploaded a short technical appendix with the API spec and sample dump here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-vf-proposal (same as attachment link). Quick answers inline:

- Auth: API key + optional mTLS for enterprise tenants; we can enable short-lived OIDC for the POC.
- SQL: we support SELECT ... FROM vectors WHERE vector_embedding <-> query ORDER BY ... LIMIT N; INSERT/UPDATE for upserts.
- QPS: for the sample index we see typical POC spikes up to 250 qps, sustained 40-60 qps. Concurrency: connectors accept 100 concurrent connections by default.
- Sample corpus: attached CSV is ~120k rows, 1536-dim vectors, avg doc size ~420 tokens.
- Cold-tier: S3 in us-west-2, presigned parallel GETs, median cold retrieval 210ms (varies with chunking, we can tune).
- KV cache interactions: the connector serves stable ids; we recommend TTL > 24h for embeddings that do not change frequently.

We also attached a short MOU (redwood-poc-mou.docx) and can prepare a DocuSign envelope to formalize the pilot scope — link here: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/embeddedSign?envelopeId=VF-POC-2026.

If that all looks good, we'll run the baseline perf first thing Monday and share raw logs for your team to inspect.

Best,
Elena
